summary: Backend-only Java/Maven verification of 3 roadmap tasks: (1) dynamic CPA-based outbound mTLS trust in OutboundSoapClient, (2) inbound OIN anti-spoofing in OrchestratorService, (3) MessageStatusReconciliationScheduler watchdog. Installed JDK 21.0.2 + Maven 3.9.9 (previous installs lost). `mvn compile` + `mvn test-compile` for ebms-common, cpa-service, ebms-orchestrator ALL SUCCESS. Wrote 3 new focused Mockito test classes (9 new tests total) + ran full non-Testcontainers suite for ebms-orchestrator: 22/22 tests PASS (all previously existing tests + 9 new). Testcontainers-based integration tests skipped (no Docker in sandbox — documented restriction). cpa-service unit tests 1/1 PASS (only integration test needs Docker).
action_items: None required for the 3 tasks under review — all compile clean, all new + existing unit tests pass.

Optional (out of scope for this session): the Testcontainers integration tests (OutboundPipelineIntegrationTest, InboundPipelineIntegrationTest, OrchestratorServiceIntegrationTest, CpaServiceIntegrationTest) still require Docker to run end-to-end incl. Flyway V4 migration on a real Postgres — verify in CI where Docker is available.
critical_code_review_comments: OutboundSoapClient: send() correctly gates the dynamic CPA cert lookup behind isHttps(); for plain http, cpaValidationService is never touched (verified by test (c)). Fail-closed contract holds: CERTIFICATE_NOT_FOUND / CPA_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE from CpaValidationService propagates unchanged (test (b)); dispatch is never reached when trust build cannot succeed.

OutboundSoapClient.buildDynamicSslContext catches everything as MTLS_TRUST_ERROR — but the initial cpaValidationService.getPartnerCertificates() call is OUTSIDE the try/catch, so its EbmsException correctly bubbles up with its original errorCode (e.g. CERTIFICATE_NOT_FOUND). Verified.

OrchestratorService.validateInboundOin: step 0 executes BEFORE cpaValidationService.validateCpaAndOin — verified by test (b) that asserts validateCpaAndOin was never called on OIN mismatch. Rejection persists a FAILED row with errorMessage set (field added via V4 migration + entity update).

OrchestratorService: on blank clientOin + enforce=true, the code correctly persists a FAILED row and throws SecurityFailure; on enforce=false, it warn-logs and continues. Verified by tests (c) and (d).

EbmsMessageProvider: the new catch (EbmsException e) block sits between DuplicateMessageException and generic Exception, and correctly maps e.getErrorCode() → soapHelper.createErrorResponse(errorCode, message, null). This means a SecurityFailure raised by validateInboundOin produces a SOAP fault with faultCode 'SecurityFailure' (not the generic 'Unknown'). Verified by code review; not covered by a dedicated unit test because the provider requires JAX-WS WebServiceContext plumbing — the existing RawPayloadCaptureInterceptorTest exercises the surrounding wiring.

MessageStatusReconciliationScheduler: threshold = Instant.now().minusSeconds(stuckProcessingTimeoutMinutes * 60L) — correct; @Scheduled fixedDelayString reads ebms.watchdog.check-interval-ms (default 300000ms). saveAll called only when the stuck list is non-empty. All verified.

EbmsMessageRepository.findStuckProcessingMessages: JPQL is syntactically valid ('SELECT m FROM EbmsMessageEntity m WHERE m.status = ''PROCESSING'' AND m.updatedAt < :threshold'). Compile-time JPA metamodel + Spring Data proxy generation succeed as part of mvn test-compile; runtime query validation happens at Hibernate SessionFactory bootstrap which is covered whenever a *IntegrationTest boots the Spring context (Testcontainers required — deferred to CI).
PartnerCertificateDto: @JsonIgnoreProperties(ignoreUnknown = true) + all fields with @Getter/@Setter make it a valid Jackson deserialization target for the cpa-service response shape.

Flyway V4 migration file syntactically OK (ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS + COMMENT). Actual apply-on-top-of-V3 will be validated whenever a Testcontainers-backed test class runs; not runnable in sandbox but the SQL is standard PostgreSQL.

Minor observation (non-blocking): OutboundSoapClient logs 'CXF HTTPConduit niet beschikbaar – fallback timeout: not a proxy instance' during the http/https tests because the JDK-based dispatch does not expose an HTTPConduit. This is the pre-existing fallback branch — no regression, message flow is unaffected. The mTLS TLSClientParameters setter path is likewise fallback-noop in a pure JDK dispatch, but the SSLContext build itself is what the test verifies.
